source.title: How many conjectures can you stand? – a survey

accepted.question_text: Does every 4-connected claw-free graph contain a Hamilton cycle, that is, a cycle passing through every vertex exactly once? Here a claw-free graph means a graph with no induced subgraph isomorphic to K1,3.

evidence.quote: Conjecture 1 Every 4-connected claw-free graph is hamiltonian.

accepted.question_text: Does every 4-connected line graph contain a Hamilton cycle? Equivalently, if a graph is the line graph L(H) of some graph H and is 4-connected, must it be hamiltonian?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 2 Every 4-connected line graph is hamiltonian.

accepted.question_text: Does every essentially 4-edge-connected graph contain a dominating closed trail, meaning a connected eulerian subgraph T such that every edge of the graph has at least one end vertex on T?
accepted.context_brief: Dominating closed trails in essentially 4-edge-connected graphs

evidence.quote: Conjecture 6 Every essentially 4-edge-connected graph has a DCT.

accepted.question_text: Does every cyclically 4-edge-connected cubic graph contain a dominating cycle, that is, a cycle meeting every edge by containing at least one of its endpoints?
accepted.context_brief: Dominating cycles in cyclically 4-edge-connected cubic graphs

evidence.quote: Conjecture 7 Every cyclically 4-edge-connected cubic graph has a DC.

accepted.question_text: Does every 4-connected 4-regular claw-free graph contain a Hamilton cycle?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 8 Every 4-connected 4-regular claw-free graph is hamiltonian.

accepted.question_text: Does every 4-connected 4-regular claw-free graph in which each vertex lies on exactly two triangles contain a Hamilton cycle?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 9 Every 4-connected 4-regular claw-free graph in which each vertex lies on exactly two triangles is hamiltonian.

accepted.question_text: Are the following two statements equivalent to the dominating-cycle conjecture for cyclically 4-edge-connected cubic graphs: (i) every such graph G has a cycle C for which G − V(C) is acyclic, and (ii) every such graph on n vertices has a cycle of length at least c n for some constant c with 0 < c < 1?

evidence.quote: We are not aware of any attempts to establishing the equivalence of these conjectures, and we leave it as an open problem.

accepted.question_text: Does every cyclically 4-edge-connected cubic graph that is not 3-edge-colorable contain a dominating cycle?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 12 Every cyclically 4-edge-connected cubic graph that is not 3-edge-colorable has a DC.

accepted.question_text: Does every snark, meaning in this paper a cyclically 4-edge-connected cubic graph of girth at least 5 that is not 3-edge-colorable, contain a dominating cycle?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 13 Every snark has a dominating cycle.

accepted.question_text: Does every cyclically 4-edge-connected cubic graph contain a weakly contractible subgraph F with minimum degree 2?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 14 Every cyclically 4-edge-connected cubic graph contains a weakly contractible subgraph F with δ(F) = 2.

accepted.question_text: Does every cyclically 4-edge-connected cubic graph G contain a weakly contractible subgraph F whose set AG(F) of attachment vertices has size at least 4?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 15 Every cyclically 4-edge-connected cubic graph G contains a weakly contractible subgraph F with |AG(F)| ≥ 4.

accepted.question_text: Is there a substantive connection between the conjectures about dominating cycles in snarks and conjectures on double cycle covers?

evidence.quote: – Is there a link to conjectures on Double Cycle Covers?

accepted.question_text: Is there a substantive connection between the conjectures about dominating cycles in snarks and conjectures on nowhere-zero flows?

evidence.quote: – Is there a link to conjectures on Nowhere-Zero Flows?

accepted.question_text: Do there exist sublinear functions f1(n) and f2(n) such that every 4-connected line graph G on n vertices contains at most f1(n) paths whose union covers at least n − f2(n) vertices of G?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 16 There are sublinear functions f1(n) and f2(n) such that every 4-connected line graph G of order n contains ≤ f1(n) paths that cover ≥ n − f2(n) vertices of G.

accepted.question_text: In every cyclically 4-edge-connected cubic graph, must any two disjoint edges lie on a single dominating cycle?
accepted.context_brief: Dominating cycle through two disjoint edges

evidence.quote: Conjecture 18 In a cyclically 4-edge-connected cubic graph any two disjoint edges are on a DC.

accepted.question_text: In every cyclically 4-edge-connected cubic graph, must any two edges, even if they are adjacent, lie on a single dominating cycle?
accepted.context_brief: Dominating cycle through any two edges

evidence.quote: Conjecture 19 In a cyclically 4-edge-connected cubic graph any two edges are on a DC.

accepted.question_text: Let H be a subgraph of an essentially 4-edge-connected cubic graph with minimum degree 2, and suppose exactly four vertices of H have degree 2. If two new edges are added pairing those four degree-2 vertices, must the resulting graph always have a dominating closed trail containing both added edges?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 20 Any subgraph H of an essentially 4-edge-connected cubic graph with δ(H) = 2 and |V2(H)| = 4 is V2(H)-dominated.

accepted.question_text: Under the same hypotheses as Conjecture 20, is every such subgraph H strongly V2(H)-dominated, meaning both the two-added-edge condition holds and, for any single added edge joining two of the degree-2 vertices, the resulting graph has a dominating closed trail containing that added edge?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 21 Any subgraph H of an essentially 4-edge-connected cubic graph with δ(H) = 2 and |V2(H)| = 4 is strongly V2(H)-dominated.

accepted.question_text: Is every 4-connected line graph of a multigraph Hamilton-connected, meaning that for every two distinct vertices there exists a Hamilton path joining them?
accepted.context_brief: Hamilton-connectedness of 4-connected line graphs of multigraphs

evidence.quote: Conjecture 22 Every 4-connected line graph of a multigraph is Hamilton-connected.

accepted.question_text: Is every 4-connected claw-free graph Hamilton-connected, meaning that between any two distinct vertices there exists a Hamilton path?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 23 Every 4-connected claw-free graph is Hamilton-connected.

accepted.question_text: Does deciding whether a graph is 1-Hamilton-connected remain NP-complete even when the input is restricted to line graphs? A positive answer would, according to the paper, imply that the conjecture asserting every 4-connected line graph is hamiltonian is false unless P = NP.

evidence.quote: It seems not unlikely that deciding whether a given graph is 1-Hamilton-connected remains NP-complete when restricted to line graphs. If one would be able to show this, however, it would imply that Conjecture 2 cannot be true, unless P=NP.

accepted.question_text: Is every 4-connected line graph of a multigraph 1-Hamilton-connected and 2-edge-Hamilton-connected, meaning respectively that deleting any one vertex still leaves Hamilton paths between arbitrary two vertices, and that after adding any one or two possible edges there is a Hamilton cycle containing all added edges?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 24 Every 4-connected line graph of a multigraph is 1-Hamilton-connected (2-edge-Hamilton-connected).

accepted.question_text: Is every 4-connected claw-free graph 1-Hamilton-connected, meaning that for any vertex x, the graph obtained by deleting x has a Hamilton path between any two remaining vertices?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 25 Every 4-connected claw-free graph is 1-Hamilton-connected.

accepted.question_text: Does every 2-edge-connected graph G contain an eulerian subgraph H with at least three edges such that every component of G − V(H) is connected to H by at most three edges?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 31 Every 2-edge-connected graph G has an eulerian subgraph H with at least three edges such that each component of G−V(H) is linked by at most three edges to H.

accepted.question_text: Can the known positive result that every 5-connected claw-free graph with minimum degree at least 6 is Hamilton-connected be strengthened to cover all 5-connected line graphs or all 5-connected claw-free graphs, without the additional minimum-degree assumption?

evidence.quote: The authors state in their concluding section of [37] that it is conceivable that a further refinement in some parts of their analysis might improve the result a bit, perhaps even to all 5-connected line (claw-free) graphs.

accepted.question_text: In the theorem stating that every 3-connected, essentially 11-connected claw-free or line graph is hamiltonian, can the essential-connectivity requirement 11 (or the improved value 9 mentioned later) be lowered further—possibly all the way to 5—and, if the ordinary connectivity requirement is raised from 3-connected to 4-connected, how far can that essential-connectivity threshold be decreased?

evidence.quote: Perhaps the 11 in Theorem 36 can be replaced by 5, which would be best possible
An open question is how far we can decrease the 11 (or 9) by raising the 3 to a 4 in the theorem.
